title: 'Loved Pup Cups': Fallen K-9 Whiskee remembered by handler - NewsBreak
text: KINGSPORT, Tenn. (WJHL) — A beloved K-9 officer of the Kingsport Police Department, Whiskee, passed away from cancer on Monday. His handler, Carrie Peters, said that through his toughness, he was well-known for his affectionate nature and love for whipped cream. “He was a ladies’ man and one of the boys,” Peters said. Whiskee served with the Kingsport Police Department (KPD) for over three years and was trained in Patrol and Narcotics Detection. He was diagnosed with cancer in 2022 and continued to work until his passing on Monday. After no veterinarian in the region could identify his type of cancer, a clinic in California discovered Whiskee had been diagnosed with a rare skin cancer. The only way to treat it was through amputation, but unfortunately, this was not an option for him. “He had a mass on his chest,” she said. Peters said that while Whiskee worked during his diagnosis, it did not slow him down. She said just two weeks ago, he protected her and five other officers during a burglary. “He could flip a switch,” she said. Peters said Whiskee’s gnarly bite earned him treats from time to time. She said after his first hit, he was offered a steak, but chose a bowl-sized Pup Cup instead. Whiskee’s friends at the KPD often turned to him for comfort after a taxing day. Peters said her fellow officers referred to their time with him as “Whiskee therapy” or, jokingly, the only “Whiskee they could have on shift.” “When we have bad days and a bunch of us have bad calls, that can put us down,” Peters said. ” I would just let him out.” Peters, who is also the first woman K-9 handler in Kingsport, told News Channel 11 that former KPD K-9 Reko inspired her. She said after seeing how Reko kept his handler safe, she knew she wanted her own. Reko served several years with the department before passing away from cancer. Whiskee was loved by his department and at home with Peters, her husband, Brett, two bonus daughters, Ryker and Rowan, and their boxer/lab mix, Raider. Peters said Whiskee loved his family and turned into the ultimate softie for them. She said a few nights ago, during a storm, Whiskee jumped into the dryer to avoid the rain. “He was like, ‘Mama, I am not going out there.'” In addition to being the tuxedo-wearing ring bearer at Peters’ wedding, Whiskee also held the honorary title of mascot for Lincoln Elementary School. Peters mentioned that one little girl dressed up as a K-9 handler for Halloween, and Whiskee and Peters surprised her with a visit on her birthday. Peters said Whiskee will be remembered for his loving personality and commitment to his handler. He was a fierce protector who loved his treats and playing tug-of-war with his Kong toys. “And he won every time.” The KPD hosted a service honoring Whiskee and his work on Wednesday. Peters said at the service that the only two people who disliked Whiskee were his two bites. News Channel 11 attended Whiskee’s service; photos are below: Whiskee: End of Watch – July 28, 2025. Peters extended a ‘thank you’ to Dr. Cherry and his staff at Cherry Point Animal Hospital for their commitment and love toward Whiskee.
